subject: unity
note: Where every volatile Unity SDK fact comes from. The pack prose must not restate a name this file can derive; it names the recipe, and extract_surface.py runs it. The source checkout is per-machine and is never recorded here.

components.why: The scene components a reader adds. Partial classes span several files, so the type name is read from the source rather than the file name. Scene-level components only; module controllers live under SDK/Modules and are covered by inspector_components.

configuration.why: Settings and profile assets a page tells a reader to create.

modules.why: One folder per feature module. A module missing from the pack is a whole documented surface the writer is blind to.

assemblies.why: The assembly a module ships as, which is what a compile error names.

menu_paths.why: A class name and its Add Component label differ often enough that guessing produces a click path that does not exist.

samples.why: Samples are referred to by their exact display name.

dependencies.why: The dependency list a compatibility page states. Versions stay in GitBook variables; only the names come from here.

types.why: Every type the package declares. This is what settles whether a name a page uses is real; the narrower sets say what a reader is meant to touch.

inspector_components.why: Types a reader can add in the Inspector. A module of these that the pack never mentions is a surface the writer is blind to.

must_not_exist_why: Names that have never existed or were renamed, and that keep reappearing in drafts because they are what a reasonable person would guess. The site check treats any page naming one of these as an error.
documented_sets_why: Sets small enough that every member matters. Ten feature modules: a missing one is a whole documented surface the writer is blind to.
coverage_sets_why: Sets the pack legitimately summarises rather than enumerates. Reported as a single ratio, because sixty-three separate warnings would bury the ten that matter.
historical_pages_why: Pages whose job is to say what changed. A retired component name on one of these is correct; treating it as drift would bury the pages that are actually wrong.
coverage_ignore_prefixes_why: Names that appear on pages but are deliberately outside the shipped package surface - sample and tutorial assets. MCP tool ids like Convai.ConfigureGaze are excluded automatically because a dotted name is never a type.
section_why: Where this subject's pages live in the documentation repository. Declared rather than inferred from the pack name: core-service's pages are under api-reference, and guessing reported its own exemplars as borrowed from another subject.
